chapter: Recording dates, Goodman and band life
title: Stuff Smith plays Humoresque for five minutes on a V-disc broadcast
summary: On a V-disc show with Milton Berle, a drinking Stuff stretched the number from two minutes to five.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: And the trio just played on there, you know? Oh, here's another funny thing about Stuff Smith. We're doing a -- what was that thing? V-disks, you know, over -- for the service.

But we would broadcast, you know. So we had a big orchestra with Paul Berry and Charlie Shavers (PEOPLE) was playing trumpet, and Trummy Young, and Teddy was playing piano, a big band, good musicians. So we would do two performances, you know, and I guess Milton Berle was the emcee at that point, on the show. So you know, you've got to

We did the first thing around, it was okay. None of us had had a drink, nothing. So we went around to the same White Rose Bar, but John and I didn't take any drinks, you know, but Stuff took some. Now, we were playing, "Humoresque." We used to have a nice little jazz thing on it. Say for instance if it went two minutes on the shot that's going over to the armed services, and then we had a local shot, you know, a national shot, you know?
Stuff-- it was two minutes the first time around. Stuff would come back and that booze told him to play for four or five minutes.

And Milton Berle was in the wings and in fact John Levy and I were talking about it the other day, you know, because I told him I was trying to find what to talk about him, and I eventually did work up on the story, you know?

And John said he wanted to hit Stuff up side of the head so bad, instead of staying orderly, you know? Stuff came back and just closed his eyes, playing the violin, closed his eyes, like he was Heifetz.
And played, "Humoresque", for five minutes. And that means somebody has to come off, somebody just gets wiped off the program.
Lionel Hampton used to do that, you know. He would start playing, "Flying Home," and play it so long in the theaters they'd have to wipe the news out.

Because he played all into the news time, you know? Had to go right back to the feature picture. So Stuff did the same thing. But it didn't hurt us, you know, didn't hurt us at all, because I heard the V-disks later and they turned out good. Both performances were good, but you still have to stay in order.
